六级大纲词汇 · 11英文原文

The Word Beside the Joke

玩笑旁边的那个词 · 589 词 · 6 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1Jo planned to reprint an anonymous pamphlet from a factory strike. An excerpt in an encyclopedia called a broken machine "the finest repair in town." His first caption accused workers of sabotage. Before publication a retired worker agreed to proofread it. She laughed at the caption and asked for the preceding sentence. Jo found the full manuscript in an archive. Its opening salutation offered condolences to a family whose son had been hurt. That made the writer's anonymity easier to understand.

2The phrase had a familiar denotation and a bitter connotation. It denoted no actual repair. The writer had used a familiar cliché to allude to a real injury. The author used sarcasm to expose the hypocrisy of an owner who praised a dangerous machine. A neighbor's autobiography included an autobiographical sketch that recalled the accident. Jo treated it as anecdotal evidence until a chronicle confirmed the date. The anecdote also made sense of a metaphor about a machine taking a rest. Its allusion to the injured boy made the praise sound different once he read the page in order.

3An ambiguous abbreviation remained in the margin. A linguistics teacher said it could signify two things. A trade directory gave the linguistic clue. Its glossary explained an affix marking a job akin to a mechanic's. A second mark denoted the machine itself. An apprentice had embedded a small drawing next to that abbreviation, making its purpose clear. The suffix was an example of affixation found in several job names. An appendix gave a synonym for an obscure tool and made the shorthand intelligible to a layman. The apparent ambiguity came from a convention that a factory worker would have understood.

4The school editor wanted a sensational headline and called the pamphlet propaganda. He wanted to censor a vulgar line on grounds of obscenity. Jo questioned that censorship. Jo asked him to read it in the context of the official notices it mocked. Jo suggested giving the passage and the accusation equal space. His concise note showed how satire made the owner's praise sound hypocritical. Readers could compare its sarcastic tone with the owner's overt praise. A query to the library took the pamphlet out of obscurity. A librarian compiled a bibliography from the records of a newspaper syndicate. It listed the compiler's credentials. It led to a meticulous compilation of strike pamphlets. The compiler's account gave Jo enough credibility to challenge his own cynical caption without identifying the anonymous author by guesswork.

5Jo's first note used so much jargon that his explanation was harder to understand than the pamphlet. The teacher asked him to articulate its point in one sentence. He replaced his elaborate and metaphorical account with a plain description of what the owner had said. The teacher said eloquence depended on clear articulation. The note posed an apt question. "What had the machine done to deserve praise?" The school printed the first caption beside the revised one as a visible refutation.

6At a factory reunion a reader asked whether the writer had been a professional satirist. Another pondered what cynicism had allowed officials to praise a dangerous machine. The retired worker said her father had saved the pamphlet because it had made him laugh at an official excuse, even in grief. Jo had taken the same line as evidence of guilt. In retrospect his interpretation had equated a joke about a machine with an attack on it. He opened his notebook and copied the words next to the joke. That was where the difference had been waiting.

六级大纲词汇 · 11中文译文

玩笑旁边的那个词

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1乔打算重印工厂罢工时期的一份匿名传单。百科全书摘录的一段话把坏掉的机器称为“全镇最棒的一次维修”。他最初写的图注指责工人故意破坏机器。刊发前，一名退休工人答应帮他校对。她看到图注就笑了，让乔找找那句话前面写了什么。乔在档案馆找到了完整手稿。开头的问候之后，是向一个孩子受伤的家庭表示慰问。作者为何不留姓名，也就更好理解了。

2那句话字面意思很平常，语气却很苦涩。它没有指一次真正的维修。作者用一句套话暗指有人受伤，又用讽刺揭露厂主的虚伪。明明机器很危险，厂主还在夸它。一位邻居在自传里回忆了事故。乔只把这当成个人回忆，直到编年记录证实了日期。这段故事也让他明白，为什么作者会把停机比成机器终于能休息。顺着原文读下去，看到它暗指受伤的孩子，那句夸奖就有了不同的意味。

3页边还有一个意思不明的缩写。一位语言学老师说，它可能指两样东西。行业名录提供了语言线索，术语表说明其中一个词缀表示类似机修工的职位，另一个符号才指机器本身。一名学徒在缩写旁画了小图，把它的意思说清楚了。这个后缀也是几个工种名称里常见的构词方式。附录还列出一件生僻工具的同义词，让外行也能看懂这种简写。原来看似模棱两可的地方，工厂里的老工人本来一看就明白。

4学校报纸的编辑想用一个轰动的标题，还说传单是在搞宣传。他认为一行话粗俗不雅，想删掉。乔质疑这种审查，请他把那行话和它所嘲讽的官方告示一起读。乔建议让传单原文和指控占同样的篇幅。他用简短的说明指出，讽刺怎样让厂主的夸奖显得虚伪。读者可以拿传单里的挖苦和厂主公开的赞扬作比较。乔向图书馆查询，这份传单才重新被人注意。馆员根据一家报业联合组织的档案编了一份书目，里面列有编者的资历，又指向一份精心整理的罢工传单汇编。编者提供的信息足以让乔质疑自己原先冷嘲热讽的图注，无须靠猜测认定匿名作者是谁。

5乔的初稿塞了太多行话，比传单还难懂。老师请他用一句话说清重点。乔把繁复的比喻换成对厂主发言的直白描述。老师说，表达清楚才能真正有说服力。短说明留给读者一个恰当的问题，那台机器究竟做了什么，值得这样的赞扬？学校把旧图注和改过的版本并排印出来，让读者一眼就看出反驳在哪里。

6在一次老工人聚会上，有人问作者是不是专业的讽刺作家。另一人琢磨，官员能夸一台危险的机器，背后是怎样的冷漠。退休工人说，她父亲把传单留下，是因为它让他在悲伤中也能笑一笑那些官方托词。乔却一度把同一句话当成工人有罪的证据。回头想想，他把拿机器开玩笑等同于袭击机器。他打开笔记本，抄下玩笑旁边的那几句话。区分两种解读的线索，一直就在那儿。
